code.summary: All of the ⚙ cog lives in one place: index.html:969-1055 holds the markup, js/app.js:8369-8850 the logic, styles.css:3640-3724 the shared and phone CSS for Canvas and Friends, styles.css:8563-8619 the PC layout of the two, and styles.css:8627-8777 the Editor block. Today it runs as a 'pair': exactly one block is big and the others are bars. There is no state with every block closed, and an open block has no visible bar, so you cannot tap it shut. The cog reopens on whichever of Canvas or Friends was open last, kept per device in localStorage 'fm.cvPair'. The Editor block is never remembered. One ⤢ markup sits in both the Canvas and Friends bars. The Editor bar has no ⤢: its 'What should you use?' button does the opening instead. 'App settings…' exists twice: #cv-appset in Canvas's Cancel/Apply row and #cv-mini-app inside the Canvas bar. Both close the cog and open the same left-hand Settings drawer, on phone and PC alike. The app has no shared icon set. The Simple and Full icons that were decided (D16 A) exist only in the design kit, as VIS.ICONS 'quick' and 'full'. Expected test fallout: the remembered-block tests turn red (945, 978, 983, 980 cog T9), as does the queue-35 #cv-appset test. Several older tests that open the cog and use the Canvas card are at risk. The biggest blocker is the Full-unchanged lock. These edits touch cv-ed lines and lines from the v17.36 Simple release, so ship.sh's gate fires and demands a full-unchanged.sh PASS. That PASS cannot come, because FU6 records the Canvas/Friends half of the cog against HEAD and this request changes exactly that. The plan needs a route through the gate, decided with Ezra.

findings.claim: (a) Layout: on a phone the blocks sit in one centred flex column, with each small block shown as a 64px bar on top. The Editor bar (order -2) comes first, then Friends (order -1), then the Canvas card. When the Editor block is open it drops to the bottom (order 1). Exactly one block is ever open: that state is two body classes on #canvas-dialog, cv-fr-big and cv-ed-big, and with neither set Canvas is open. There is no 'all closed' state.

findings.claim: (a) Which block opens with the cog: the cog calls openCanvasDialog({block:'last'}), and that reads localStorage 'fm.cvPair' ('friends', otherwise 'canvas'). The key is per device and never goes in the project. It is written on every swap except to the Editor block. Other ways in pick their own block: the person+ / people chip / LIVE / Home's Share live open Friends, and the oversize warning (a bare call) opens Canvas.

findings.claim:
(b) The shared ⤢ is a 38px round button.cv-mini-exp, the last thing in each bar. It has no listener of its own: a click bubbles to the bar's listener, which calls cvPairSwap(name). 'Open big' (cvPairSwap) works like this:
- It runs a FLIP flight: measure every block, change state, then animate each block from its old box to its new one over 460ms while bar and content cross-fade.
- The tapped block becomes big and the others become bars.
- It remembers Canvas or Friends in fm.cvPair.
- Friends' content is drawn only while Friends is big (U.renderFriends) and cleared on settle.
- Focus returns to the shrinking block's expand control.
- With reduced motion the swap is instant.
- It returns early when the tapped block is already big.

CSS at styles.css:3672-3675 (38px, ::before inset -6px gives a 50px catch, svg 17px). Listeners at js/app.js:8600-8601 (`cvFrBar ... cvPairSwap('friends')`, `cvMini ... cvPairSwap('canvas')`) and js/app.js:8439 (Editor bar). cvPairSwap at js/app.js:8539-8599: early return at 8540 `|| cvPairBig() === to) return;`, the EXP refocus map at 8555 `{ canvas: 'cv-mini-exp', friends: 'cv-fr-exp', editor: 'cv-ed-what' }`, the reduced-motion path at 8562, DUR 460 at 8580. aria-expanded is kept in cvPairApply at js/app.js:8510-8515. The flight CSS is styles.css:3693-3699 and 8648-8652.

findings.claim:
(c) The Editor block's small bar is built in JS, div.cv-mini#cv-ed-bar. It holds, in order:
1. span.ed-head: the ED_ICON icon plus the title 'Editor', which the phone hides.
2. button.ed-sw, the Simple/Full pill: knob span.ed-k, word 'Simple', a '⇄' glyph, word 'Full'. Its aria-label and title name the action ('Switch to Simple editor').
3. span.ed-gap.
4. button.ed-what#cv-ed-what, 'What should you use?' (aria-expanded).

The switch stops propagation and calls FM.editor.request. After a switch the cog closes unless Canvas has unapplied picks or Friends is open. 'What should you use?' has no listener of its own: it bubbles to the bar, which calls cvPairSwap('editor'). That opens the explanation (#cv-ed-body), which contains:
- the title 'What should you use?'
- a big switch with words, plus 'You’re in Full'
- two option cards drawn from ED_PIC
- the note line
- a refusal line (#cv-ed-why)

The words come from js/spine-words.js:12-19. The small and big switch come from one function, edSwitch(big). So an icons-only small switch with a still-worded big one needs just a branch on `big`.

The phone wraps .ed-what into two lines, max-width 112px (styles.css:8676-8677), and the ≤359px rules at 8679-8684 shrink things further. The short-screen PC/sideways height constant is CV_ED_COL = 159+10+216 (js/app.js:8471), which assumes today's Editor tile height of 159 px.

findings.claim:
(d) 'App settings…' exists twice:
1. #cv-appset, left-aligned in the Canvas card's action row beside Cancel/Apply. It is visible only while Canvas is open.
2. #cv-mini-app, a small pill on the Canvas bar's title line, added by #967 B2 so Settings stays reachable while Friends is open. It stops propagation and clicks #cv-appset.

Both close the cog (cvClose, which also un-pins the PC anchor) and then call FM.settings.open(). That opens the same app-wide Settings panel on phone and PC: a left slide-in drawer min(380px, 88vw) wide, full height, z 220. In a project it leads with 'Save a project file' and 'Reports from this device'. A plain open() sets no return trip, so closing Settings does not reopen the cog, though openAt(…,{onClose}) exists. On Home the cog opens Settings directly.

findings.claim:
(f) On a PC, wider than 700px, the same blocks hang off the PC cog #btn-settings in the transport row. cvPlace sets CSS variables for where the cog is, opens upward or downward by room (cv-up), and lifts the cog above the blur. Two layouts follow:
- Side by side (cv-side, when the cog's right edge ≥ 562px): a grid with one 360px open block and 176px tiles. With the Editor block it is two columns and two rows (areas 'ed cv'/'fr cv'), with Canvas always beside the cog.
- Stacked (otherwise): small blocks away from the cog, the open one next to it, each cap minus 152px.

The 'strip' is D24 B's short-screen form (cv-ed-short). When the room on the open side is under CV_ED_COL (385px), the Editor's small form becomes a pill of two controls on the cog's own row (switch + 'What should you use?'). It is not a grid item, so Canvas and Friends keep their rects.

The comic tail aims at the block next to the cog (always Canvas when side by side). #983 removed the PC Share button, so the cog is the only PC door. A width crossing re-hangs the blocks (cvOnWidth). Every one of these grids assumes exactly one 360px open block, so 'all closed' and a fourth App settings tile each need a new PC arrangement drawn as options.

findings.claim:
(g) The app has no shared icon set, sprite or icon function. Every control carries its own inline SVG string, and inspector.js has only a local svgIcon(path) helper. The only Simple/Full drawings in the app are ED_PIC: 64×34 miniatures in the explanation, too wide for a 24px icon. The icons decided for this job (D16 A: 'three clips side by side = Simple, three staggered layer bars = Full') exist only in the design kit's VIS.ICONS, at 24px with 1.8 stroke. Phase 2's plan says it ships exactly those paths. A grep for the 'quick' icon's path found it in no app file.

Useful kit names:
- 'quick' (Simple)
- 'full' / 'editor' (Full, the same path)
- 'edblock' (the Editor block)
- 'expand' (⤢)
- 'swap'
- 'gear' (a possible App settings bar icon)

The app's real gear SVG is on #btn-settings and #m-settings in index.html.

findings.claim:
(h) The Full-unchanged lock is the real blocker. Any edit here fires ship.sh's gate:
- rule 3: an added or removed line matching the hook `cv-ed(?:itor\b|-)`, which cvPairBig, cvPairApply, the EXP map and the whole Editor CSS block all contain;
- rule 5: changed lines whose git blame is the v17.36 Simple release (f7ec250c).

Once the gate fires, the release must be labelled queue 980 alone and needs a full-unchanged.sh PASS of this tree against HEAD. That run takes about three hours. It cannot pass, because FU6 records every cog element except #cv-editor at 14 sizes: the dialog's classes, the aria-expanded values, the state after reopening, and the Cancel/Apply/swap behaviour. FU1 also screenshots the cog. All-closed-on-open, losing #cv-appset and a new App settings block change exactly those. FU7 still finds `#cv-editor .ed-sw` on a cog with every block closed.

So the plan needs a route chosen with Ezra. Either Full's half (App settings bar, all closed, tap to close, #cv-appset removed) ships first as an ordinary release that touches no hook or Simple-written line, which is probably impractical here. Or an instrument release (`INSTRUMENT CHANGE:` / `LOOSENS THE LOCK: <his words>` in POLISH-LOG) teaches FU6 the new sanctioned cog first. His 1 Oct rule ('i dont want the original editor changing in design and function') is what this request now asks to change for the cog.

FU7's switch lookup is at tests/full-unchanged.html:3048. Priced sizes are at tools/_fu_compare.py:180-206.

findings.claim:
Constraints for the plan: on a phone a fourth (App settings) bar costs 76px from the open block's height cap. Every block closed fits easily. The Editor bar's tap targets and hit tests depend on ids that tests use, and the standing design rule applies.

Cap with three bars today: 100svh-260 (about 407px at 380×667). A fourth bar makes it 100svh-336: about 331px at 380×667, 232px at 320×568 and 217px at 375×553. The Canvas card would scroll, with its sticky Cancel/Apply, inside that room. All four closed: 4×66 + 3×10 = 294px, which fits at 320×568 (460px available).

Keeping id 'cv-ed-what' on the new Editor ⤢ (or updating the EXP map at js/app.js:8555, the hadExp check at 8552 and the tests above) avoids silent focus and test breakage. The App settings block opens Settings rather than growing, so whether its button is a ⤢ or a 'leaves' chevron is a design call.

CLAUDE.md requires drawn options before shipping: the PC all-closed and four-block arrangement, the collapse glyph for an open block's bar, the Simple/Full icons at 24px, and the App settings bar. The memory note 'review-before-shipping-storage' calls for a review lens on band/menu changes.

hist.summary:
I only read files; nothing was edited. Paths below are relative to \\wsl.localhost\ubuntu\home\ezra\FreeMotion.

(1) Which block opens: in #944/#945 (26 Sep) Ezra asked for Canvas big on first open and for the cog to come back to the last block he used. That shipped in v17.04 and was carried to PC by #978 ("the cog reopens on the last block (per device, like the phone)", REQUESTS.md:34254). The Simple plan made a deliberate exception: the Editor block is never remembered (DESIGN.md §21 F7), so the cog reopens on the last of Canvas and Friends. There has never been an all-closed state, and tapping the open block does nothing today (js/app.js:8540).

(2) What the small Editor block shows: COG-DESIGN.md §3.1 sets it. On the phone it is a 64 px bar with the icon, a "Simple ⇄ Full" switch and a two-line "What should / you use?" button, with no title. On PC it is a 176×159 tile with the icon, the word "Editor", the switch and the button.

(3) "What should you use?" comes from his own 1 Oct words. It is the button that opens the Editor block big with the explanation. So his new ask reverses that 1 Oct wording, and the all-closed ask reverses his #944 wording.

(4) App settings was never its own block. It is a button in the Canvas card's action row, added in v6.13 when the PC cog was changed to open Canvas settings. A copy on the Canvas bar was added in v17.08 (#967 batch 2, audit item J3-9), built to the recommended pick, not his words.

#970 is not a cog item (it is a hunt bug about the ⋯ button). #983 removed the PC Share button because "the settings cog has it now".

(5) The lock: it leaves #cv-editor out of every record and picture and compares everything else in #canvas-dialog. The measured price (tools/full-unchanged-price.json) is only used when the tree adds the block and HEAD has none. HEAD (v17.37) already has the block, so the price is dormant and the cog is compared exactly at every size.

(6) Release type: changes inside the Editor block (an expand button, icons on the switch) touch Simple code and lines v17.36 wrote. That makes them a Simple release: its POLISH-LOG line names only queue 980, it ships alone, and it needs a PASS on its exact tree. They can pass only if the Canvas, Friends and switch boxes outside the block do not move.

The other changes (App settings as its own block, the button gone from Canvas, all blocks closed on open, tap to close, no reopen-on-last) move or remove elements outside #cv-editor and change its classes and open/closed flags. FU6, FU1's cog screen and FU4's Friends record would all read NOT PASS. The price format cannot express any of that, and the tool that writes the price refuses once HEAD has the block. So re-pricing is not possible with the current lock. It would first need a lock-only release that changes no app file, carries "INSTRUMENT CHANGE:" and "LOOSENS THE LOCK:" in its POLISH-LOG line, gets its own PASS, and then a new price measured on this laptop. A Full-only release that touches no Simple code, no line a Simple release wrote and no lock file would not trigger the gate, but closing the Editor block too means changing lines v17.36 wrote.

findings.claim: The current price format cannot express the requested Full-side changes, so the FU4/FU6 records cannot simply be re-priced. A price can only allow box moves and changes in flight distances. A new or removed element, a restyled element, and any change to the dialog's classes, focus or open/closed flags are always reported. The tool that writes the price refuses when HEAD already has #cv-editor or when a move falls outside the four priced sizes.

It reads as 'one track of clips' against 'a stack of layers', the same idea as the ED_PIC miniatures in the explanation he opens with ⤢. The two shapes differ strongly in silhouette (a horizontal row against a staggered column), which matters at 20px.

icon_options.full_icon: The same kit 'full' staggered three bars as in A.
icon_options.why: It reuses the Full path from A unchanged, and 'one layer against many' is the simplest possible contrast. The risk: a lone bar at 20px can read as a minus sign or a slider track rather than 'Simple', which makes it weaker than A on its own.
